catalog_quote: 2.3.7 STRESS. Tindal stress is almost always penultimate, but occurs word-finally in some words with final heavy syllables. Emphasis seems to cause stress to become word-final. This is problematic for my data, because many of the forms have been elicited in isolation, and words in isolation are often emphasized. Word-final stress appears to be permitted only on heavy syllables, but not all such syllables take final stress. Example (62) illustrates instances of penultimate stress, whereas (63) shows final stress. (62) hinómbo 'where, which one' / morobúat 'to work' / tánay 'termite' (63) tanayón 'termite infested' / tompiós 'hairy caterpillar' [non-syllabic mark under the i in the original] / gipán 'centipede, scorpion' / waláy 'house' / duláʔ 'saliva' / lapáp 'sole of foot' [printed p. 9] ... new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (33 pp., text layer, ScholarSpace hdl 10125/73202 = UHWPL 36(5), open access; metadata re-confirmed online). extracted text of PDF p. 11 (header '9') contains exactly: '2.3.7 STRESS. Tindal stress is almost always penultimate, but occurs word-finally in some words with final heavy syllables. Emphasis seems to cause stress to become word-final. This is problematic for my data, because many of the forms have been elicited in isolation, and words in isolation are often emphasized. Word-final stress appears to be permitted only on heavy syllables, but not all such syllables take final stress. Example (62) illustrates instances of penultimate stress, whereas (63) shows final stress.' follow…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable by default; a minority of words with a heavy (closed or long/diphthongal) final syllable carry final stress instead, and emphatic/citation pronunciation tends to shift stress to the final syllable. The author also attributes the prepenultimate /a/ > /o/ neutralization to stress being 'nearly always penultimate' (sec. 2.3.6).
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress on some words with heavy final syllables (examples 63: tanayon, tompios, gipan, walay, dula, lapap, marked with acute accent in the original); not all heavy finals take it; emphasis (words elicited in isolation) seems to move stress to the final syllable. Loanwords discussed separately (sec. 2.4) without stress comment.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based largely on forms elicited in isolation from one speaker; author explicitly warns that isolation/emphasis may induce final stress, so citation-form vs. phrase-medial behaviour is not separated.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Tindal Dusun of Kota Belud (speaker from Kelawat district), i.e. Tempasuk Dusun, which Glottolog 5.1 lists as dialect temp1235 of Kadazan Dusun cent2100 (former ISO [tdu], merged into [dtp] by ISO 639-3 CR 2015-060). Robinson calls it 'a coastal dialect of Central Dusunic'. It is not a description of the standard Bundu-Liwan (Central Dusun) or Penampang Coastal Kadazan (coas1294) varieties; the primary phonology for those, Miller 1993, could not be opened. Based on one consultant, elicitation through English; the working-paper series asks readers to note its preliminary nature.

new_statements.quote: 3. Stress. Tindal stress is almost always penultimate, but occurs word-finally in some words with final heavy syllables. Emphasis seems to cause stress to become word-final. This is problematic for my data, because many of the forms have been elicited in isolation, and words in isolation are often emphasized. Word-final stress appears to be permitted only on heavy syllables, but not all such syllables take final stress. Example (5) illustrates instances of penultimate stress, whereas (6) shows final stress. (5) hinómbo 'where, which one', morobúat 'to work', tánay 'termite' (6) tanayón 'termite infested', tompiós 'hairy caterpillar', gipán 'centipede, scorpion', waláy 'house', dulá 'saliva', lapáp 'sole of foot'

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: text layer). Sec. 3 'Stress' is on PDF p. 2 as stated; the prose ('Tindal stress is almost always penultimate, but occurs word-finally in some words with final heavy syllables. Emphasis seems to cause stress to become word-final.. Word-final stress appears to be permitted only on heavy syllables, but not all such syllables take final stress. Example (5) illustrates instances of penultimate stress, whereas (6) shows final stress.') is verbatim. Minor differences: the stress marks in examples (5)-(6) are a non-embedded legacy-font glyph (text layer 'hinoÛmbo', 'tanayoÛn'; rendered page shows a double-arrow glyph), which the reader normalised to acute accents (hinómbo, tanayón etc.); the mark…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penultimate) and word-for-word the same statement as the existing Robinson 2005 sec. 2.3.7 quote; the six listed final-stress exceptions and the remark that penultimate stress conditions prepenultimate /a/ > /o/ are the only additions. Describes Tindal (Tempasuk Dusun, Glottolog temp1235, a dialect under cent2100), from a single speaker.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable almost always; some words with a heavy (closed or diphthong-final) final syllable take final stress instead, but not every heavy final syllable attracts it, and emphasis (including citation-form elicitation) can shift stress to the final syllable. Sec. 5 adds that penultimate stress conditions the neutralization of prepenultimate /a/ to /o/.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress in some words with heavy final syllables (six examples given: tanayón, tompiós, gipán, waláy, dulá, lapáp); emphasis shifts stress to the final syllable; the author notes her isolation-elicited data may over-represent final stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Robinson items describe Tindal (Tempasuk) Dusun, Glottolog temp1235, a dialect under cent2100, from a single speaker resident in Hawai'i. Hurlbut 1979 describes the Labuk dialect of Kadazan (Kamansi, mouth of the Labuk River; Wonod upriver), which Glottolog files as Labuk-Kinabatangan Kadazan labu1249 [dtb], not cent2100; its listing under cent2100 in the catalog appears to be a misattachment.
